# Scaled-residual held-out regression fixtures

These two FP32 evaluation checkpoints come from the frozen transformer lab
cohort `experiments/residual_generalization`, training commit `e4edb9f5`.
Both declared scaling-control seeds are included; neither was selected by final
test performance. The source GPT model at `ad76812` reproduces every saved test
prediction from the independent lab implementation. SHA256 hashes and the frozen
protocol identifier are in `manifest.json`. Archives use NumPy arrays without
pickle and contain evaluation weights, held-out rows, and training input pairs.

| Initialization seed | Updates | Correct unseen pairs | Test accuracy | Scaling disabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 11 | 23000 | 2276 / 2328 | 97.77% | 843 / 2328 (36.21%) |
| 17 | 23000 | 2290 / 2328 | 98.37% | 1019 / 2328 (43.77%) |

The model is width 128, depth 4, four heads, exact source RoPE/QK normalization,
centered XSA, Peri-RMSNorm, SwiGLU and tied readout. Branch coefficients are
`1/sqrt(2*depth)` after the branch output normalization. Training used only
Schedule-Free AdamW, Python 3.15/Torch 2.15 and fullgraph CUDA max-autotune.
Training pairs were half of the P97 division table; validation and final test
were disjoint quarters. The final test was first scored after learning closed.
The test independently checks the modular labels and train/test input separation.

At the same 23,000 updates, validation scores were 97.60%/98.37% for scaling and
34.97%/27.23% for ordinary addition. The scaled runs were time-censored before
the predeclared 99.9% stability criterion. Ordinary addition later reached 99.96%
final test accuracy in both seeds. Thus scaling showed earlier generalization
in this small comparison, not proven superiority at the final target.

The regression protects the already learned held-out function and rejects a
broken control that disables scaling. It does not retrain the network, guarantee
future convergence speed, or replace the full learning curves. The canonical
full optimizer/sampler states remain with the lab cohort; these evaluation
fixtures are not continuation checkpoints. Explicit regeneration uses the lab's
`review/export_scaled_regression.py` and requires its frozen data/checkpoints and
the pinned GPT model source. Expected labels are never generated by the model
under test. Both FP64 (fixed FP32 RMS epsilon) and CPU/CUDA replay agreed on the
cohort's classification predictions/counts.
